questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Ride close to the vehicle in front to use their headlights.
Slow down to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and stay flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: What is the best way to make your motorcycle visible to others?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Make eye contact with drivers.
Wave at drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: How does one alcoholic drink affect riding?

options.text: It will not result in a DUI conviction.
It will never affect your riding skills.
It can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect how well you ride. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol is below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
It marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Clothing that feels uncomfortable.
Clothing that protects you in a crash.
Clothing that does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash, keep you comfortable, and help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to protect you?

options.text: Fasten securely to your helmet.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Prevent wearing eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely to your helmet.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane without knowing you are there.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
To watch for pedestrians ahead.
To look for dark clouds that mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors when stopping to make sure drivers behind you are paying attention to you. This helps you know if they will stop safely.

questions.question: Which material gives the best crash protection?

options.text: Denim
Leather or synthetic materials
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash. Riders should wear long pants and jackets.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: Why is it hard to ride right after rain starts?

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
The road surface becomes very slippery.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road surface becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery right after rain starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, mixing with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to increase distance ahead.
Ignore them.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to increase distance ahead.
questions.explanation: Encourage tailgaters to pass by changing lanes or slowing down. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
The drinker's height
The temperature outside

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by three main factors: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: Your boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be below your ankles.
Cover your ankles.
Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding because the danger has passed.
Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: Pull off the road and check for tire and rim damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt before continuing.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Secure footing prevents your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: What should you do when lights are flashing at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
Go ahead carefully.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road in front of the motorcycle.
Not be willing to move to avoid a hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road to spot hazards early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds down the road to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: To avoid a collision, look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Goggles, glasses with impact-resistant lenses, or a helmet with a face shield:

options.text: Must be worn if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
Are optional if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
Must be worn only if you are under 21 years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be worn if your motorcycle does not have a windshield.
questions.explanation: By law, you must wear goggles, impact-resistant glasses, or a face shield helmet if your motorcycle has no windshield. A full-face helmet offers the best protection.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:

options.text: Gets better.
Stays the same.
Gets worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets worse.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces the skills needed to ride safely. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Stay close to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the part of your lane where other drivers will see you first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medicines are not very strong.
Is always safe to do.
May affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, can make it unsafe to ride. Ask your doctor how any new medicine may affect your ability to ride.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than using either one alone.
Cancel each other out.
Can be stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many medicines can impair your riding. Some medicines become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Should let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper eye or face protection. A good face shield protects your face and lets you see to both sides clearly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle's safety:

options.text: Before every ride.
Every week.
Once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.
